subject.title: fix(agents): wake top-level requester when its last parallel child settles

question: Must top-level requester-settle delivery survive a process restart during a delete-mode parallel wave, or is the documented process-local degradation acceptable for this release?
rationale: The patch fixes steady-state and shutdown-admission races, but choosing process-local versus durable ownership determines whether the original message-delivery guarantee holds across restart and affects the appropriate implementation boundary.

options.title: Require durable settle state
options.body: Persist or retain the wave's settle obligation and findings until terminal requester delivery, with a restart regression proving the final wake cannot be skipped.

options.title: Accept process-local degradation
options.body: Merge the current bounded ledger while explicitly accepting that a restart can lose the complete wave and potentially suppress a final delivered-child wake.

options.title: Pause for lifecycle redesign
options.body: Hold this PR until the broader subagent cleanup and durable-state model can represent requester-settle batches without a parallel ledger.

recommendation.title: Require durable settle state
recommendation.body: Persist or retain the wave's settle obligation and findings until terminal requester delivery, with a restart regression proving the final wake cannot be skipped.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent agent-lifecycle and gateway work-admission history makes this the strongest available owner for the restart and quiescence contract.
